## Your budget

You have 5 minutes and 40 tool calls for this task. A grep costs about 5
seconds, a test run can cost 30. Call get_status to see what remains.

Spend at most a third of your budget locating the code. Once you have a
plausible diagnosis, edit the source — a wrong patch scores the same as no
patch, so an unverified fix always beats an unfinished investigation. If
get_status shows half your time gone and you have not yet edited a source
file, stop investigating and make your best edit now.

## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Edit the source first. Only write a reproduction script once you have made
your edit and submitted it, and only if budget remains to run it.

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — everything left
in /workspace becomes your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py or
pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

The harness truncates what you receive: 5,000 characters from any command,
and 150 lines or 10,000 characters from read_file. A truncated result loses
information silently, so a broad read wastes a call AND leaves you guessing.

Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Then read_file with a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole
file and never cat one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

def get_openapi_security_definitions(
    flat_dependant: Dependant,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    security_definitions = {}
    # Use a dict to merge scopes for same security scheme
    operation_security_dict: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for security_dependency in flat_dependant._security_dependencies:
        security_definition = jsonable_encoder(
            security_dependency._security_scheme.model,
            by_alias=True,
            exclude_none=True,
        )
        security_name = security_dependency._security_scheme.scheme_name
        security_definitions[security_name] = security_definition
        # Merge scopes for the same security scheme
        if security_name not in operation_security_dict:
            operation_security_dict[security_name] = []
        for scope in security_dependency.oauth_scopes or []:
            if scope not in operation_security_dict[security_name]:
                operation_security_dict[security_name].append(scope)
    operation_security = [
        {name: scopes} for name, scopes in operation_security_dict.items()
    ]
    return security_definitions, operation_security
